metadata.title: Application Binary Interface (ABI) Knowledge Graph
metadata.description: Detailed directed knowledge graph for ABI concepts, calling conventions, data layout, symbols and linking, object formats, language ABIs, operating-system interfaces, embedded ABIs, compatibility, testing, and ABI evolution.

source_basis.title: Application binary interface article supplied by user
source_basis.coverage_used: ABI versus API; binary-level interface; ISA and register details; data sizes/layout/alignment; calling conventions; stack organization; registers; stack cleanup; unwinding; name mangling; exception propagation; system calls; object formats; embedded ABIs; C and C++ ABIs; library ABI; Linux/LSB/System V and Windows examples; ARM floating-point ABI distinctions.

source_basis.title: Supplemental ABI engineering knowledge
source_basis.coverage_used: Expanded linker/loader mechanics, ELF/PE/Mach-O components, C++ object model, FFI, runtime startup, compatibility testing, symbol/version management, interop design, and ABI-risk workflows.

metadata.id_convention: Lowercase snake_case entity IDs derived from canonical names; sequential relationship IDs use rel_00001 style.
metadata.relationship_direction: All relationships are directed from source to target. Reverse relationships are not implied.
metadata.scope_note: Conceptual, cross-platform ABI knowledge graph. Concrete ABI details vary by ISA, operating system, compiler, runtime, language, and ABI version; this graph is not a substitute for a target ABI specification.

entities.name: Application binary interface (ABI)
entities.description: Low-level contract governing how compiled machine code interacts with other code, libraries, runtime services, and the operating system.

entities.name: Application programming interface (API)
entities.description: Source-level interface describing declarations and operations available to source code before compilation.

entities.name: ABI compatibility
entities.description: Ability for separately compiled components to interact correctly under the same binary contract.

entities.name: API compatibility
entities.description: Ability for source consumers to continue using an interface, subject to source-language and build constraints.

entities.name: Binary compatibility
entities.description: Ability to run or link existing binaries without recompilation under specified platform conditions.

entities.name: Source compatibility
entities.description: Ability to rebuild existing source code against a changed interface.

entities.name: ABI stability
entities.description: Preservation of binary-level conventions across versions or releases.

entities.name: ABI break
entities.description: Incompatible change to a binary-visible contract, potentially preventing linking or correct execution.

entities.name: ABI specification
entities.description: Normative or descriptive document defining binary conventions and platform requirements.

entities.name: ABI implementation
entities.description: Compiler, runtime, library, operating system, and toolchain behavior that realizes an ABI.

entities.name: Target platform
entities.description: Combination of ISA, operating system, object format, runtime, and conventions targeted by a binary.

entities.name: Instruction set architecture (ISA)
entities.description: Programmer-visible machine instruction and architectural-state contract used by generated machine code.

entities.name: Microarchitecture
entities.description: Internal processor implementation; generally not the ABI contract itself.

entities.name: Toolchain
entities.description: Compiler, assembler, linker, libraries, and related tools used to produce binaries.

entities.name: Compiler
entities.description: Translates source or intermediate representation into machine code and ABI-conforming interfaces.

entities.name: Assembler
entities.description: Converts assembly language into object code and associated metadata.

entities.name: Linker
entities.description: Combines object files, resolves symbols, applies relocations, and creates executable or library artifacts.

entities.name: Loader
entities.description: Maps executable and library segments into a process and prepares execution.

entities.name: Operating system
entities.description: Provides process, memory, system-call, and library services used by applications.

entities.name: Runtime library
entities.description: Provides language/runtime support routines and often participates in ABI conventions.

entities.name: C library
entities.description: Provides common C runtime and operating-system-facing interfaces on many platforms.

entities.name: Standard library
entities.description: Library implementation providing language-standard facilities; its binary surface can be ABI-sensitive.

entities.name: Dynamic linker
entities.description: Resolves dynamic dependencies and symbols when a program is loaded or during execution.

entities.name: Static linking
entities.description: Copies required library code into an executable or linked artifact at build time.

entities.name: Dynamic linking
entities.description: Resolves references to shared libraries at load time or runtime.

entities.name: Shared library
entities.description: Reusable dynamically linked library exposing symbols and binary interfaces.

entities.name: Static library
entities.description: Archive of object files linked into another artifact.

entities.name: Executable
entities.description: Runnable program artifact whose machine code, object format, ABI, and dependencies must match its environment.

entities.name: Object file
entities.description: Compiled unit containing code, data, symbols, relocations, and metadata.

entities.name: Object file format
entities.description: Container specification for executable and object artifacts, symbols, sections, relocations, and metadata.

entities.name: ELF
entities.description: Executable and Linkable Format used by many Unix-like systems.

entities.name: PE/COFF
entities.description: Portable Executable and Common Object File Format used in Windows ecosystems and related toolchains.

entities.name: Mach-O
entities.description: Object and executable format used by Apple operating systems.

entities.name: Wasm module format
entities.description: Binary format for WebAssembly modules, a virtual instruction target rather than a native platform ABI by itself.

entities.name: Symbol table
entities.description: Mapping between names and symbol definitions, references, binding, visibility, and types.

entities.name: Symbol
entities.description: Named function, object, or other entity referenced by compiled components.

entities.name: Symbol resolution
entities.description: Process of matching references to symbol definitions.

entities.name: Symbol visibility
entities.description: Rules determining which symbols are exposed to other link units or dynamic consumers.

entities.name: Symbol versioning
entities.description: Mechanism allowing multiple compatible or versioned symbol interfaces to coexist.

entities.name: Name mangling
entities.description: Encoding source-language names and signatures into linker-visible symbol names.

entities.name: Demangling
entities.description: Reconstructing readable source-like names from mangled symbols.

entities.name: Relocation
entities.description: Adjustment of address-dependent fields by a linker or loader.

entities.name: Relocation entry
entities.description: Object-file record describing a location and relocation operation.

entities.name: Position-independent code (PIC)
entities.description: Code generated to execute correctly regardless of its load address, within defined constraints.

entities.name: Procedure linkage table (PLT)
entities.description: ELF mechanism commonly used for indirect calls to dynamically resolved functions.

entities.name: Global offset table (GOT)
entities.description: ELF table commonly used to access addresses of global data and dynamic symbols.

entities.name: Calling convention
entities.description: Rules for argument passing, return values, register preservation, stack use, and call/return behavior.

entities.name: Function call
entities.description: Control transfer to a function under the calling convention.

entities.name: Function return
entities.description: Transfer back to the caller while producing specified return results.

entities.name: Argument passing
entities.description: Rules for assigning parameters to registers, stack locations, or other agreed locations.

entities.name: Return value convention
entities.description: Rules for conveying function results in registers, memory, or special mechanisms.

entities.name: Caller-saved register
entities.description: Register whose value a caller must preserve if needed across a call.

entities.name: Callee-saved register
entities.description: Register whose value a callee must restore if it modifies it.

entities.name: Volatile register
entities.description: Register whose value is not guaranteed to survive a call under the convention.

entities.name: Nonvolatile register
entities.description: Register whose value must be preserved across calls under the convention.

entities.name: Stack frame
entities.description: Per-call region for locals, saved state, spill slots, and other call-related data.

entities.name: Call stack
entities.description: Stack discipline supporting nested calls, returns, and often local storage.

entities.name: Stack pointer
entities.description: Register or architectural state identifying the current stack position.

entities.name: Frame pointer
entities.description: Optional register used to reference a stack frame consistently.

entities.name: Stack alignment
entities.description: Required alignment of the stack at specified points such as function entry or call sites.

entities.name: Red zone
entities.description: ABI-defined region below the stack pointer that may be used without adjusting the stack pointer on some platforms.

entities.name: Shadow space / home space
entities.description: Caller-reserved stack area used by some conventions for register-passed arguments.

entities.name: Variadic function
entities.description: Function accepting a variable number of arguments, requiring ABI-defined argument classification and retrieval.

entities.name: Aggregate return
entities.description: Rules for returning structures, unions, or other aggregate values.

entities.name: Hidden structure-return pointer
entities.description: Implicit pointer used by some ABIs when an aggregate result is returned indirectly.

entities.name: Register classification
entities.description: Rules classifying types and assigning argument/result pieces to registers or memory.

entities.name: Parameter classification
entities.description: ABI algorithm assigning parameters to integer, floating-point, vector, or memory locations.

entities.name: Tail call
entities.description: Call optimization replacing the current frame or return path under ABI-compatible conditions.

entities.name: Unwind information
entities.description: Metadata used to reconstruct frames and restore state during unwinding.

entities.name: Stack unwinding
entities.description: Walking or dismantling call frames to propagate exceptions or restore saved execution state.

entities.name: setjmp/longjmp
entities.description: C facilities for saving and restoring a nonlocal execution context subject to platform rules.

entities.name: Exception propagation
entities.description: Binary protocol for transferring exceptions across frames and possibly across module boundaries.

entities.name: Exception handling ABI
entities.description: Conventions for exception objects, personality routines, unwind tables, and cleanup.

entities.name: Personality routine
entities.description: Language/runtime-specific logic consulted by an unwinder to decide cleanup and handler actions.

entities.name: Unwind table
entities.description: Metadata describing how to restore caller state and traverse stack frames.

entities.name: Debug information
entities.description: Metadata mapping machine code and data back to source-level constructs.

entities.name: Debug symbol
entities.description: Symbol or metadata used by debuggers to identify code and data.

entities.name: Foreign function interface (FFI)
entities.description: Mechanism allowing code in one language to call functions or exchange data with another.

entities.name: Language binding
entities.description: Language-specific wrapper or declaration exposing another language's API.

entities.name: C ABI
entities.description: Common binary contract used by C-compiled code and often adopted as an interoperability baseline.

entities.name: C++ ABI
entities.description: Binary conventions for C++ entities, including mangling, object layout, virtual dispatch, RTTI, and exceptions.

entities.name: Rust ABI
entities.description: Rust's native ABI is generally not a stable cross-version contract; extern ABI declarations select interoperability conventions.

entities.name: extern "C"
entities.description: C++ or Rust-style declaration selecting a C-compatible calling/interface convention where supported.

entities.name: Fortran ABI
entities.description: Compiler and platform conventions for Fortran procedures, data representation, and interoperability.

entities.name: Objective-C runtime ABI
entities.description: Binary/runtime conventions for Objective-C classes, selectors, messages, and metadata.

entities.name: Swift ABI
entities.description: Swift binary interface conventions; stability guarantees depend on platform and language/runtime version.

entities.name: Java Native Interface (JNI)
entities.description: Standard interface for Java code and native libraries.

entities.name: .NET P/Invoke
entities.description: Mechanism for .NET code to invoke native functions with specified marshalling and calling conventions.

entities.name: WebAssembly tool conventions
entities.description: Conventions for module imports/exports, calling, memory, and interoperability in WebAssembly environments.

entities.name: JVM bytecode
entities.description: Virtual instruction representation executed by JVM implementations; distinct from a native machine-code ABI.

entities.name: Data model
entities.description: Mapping of language types such as int, long, pointer, and size_t to widths and representations.

entities.name: Primitive type size
entities.description: ABI-defined size of fundamental scalar types.

entities.name: Type alignment
entities.description: Required alignment of a type or object in memory.

entities.name: Data layout
entities.description: Rules for field offsets, padding, aggregate alignment, and representation.

entities.name: Structure layout
entities.description: Ordering and offsets of structure fields, including padding and alignment.

entities.name: Union layout
entities.description: Storage and alignment rules for overlapping union members.

entities.name: Padding
entities.description: Unused bytes inserted to meet alignment or layout requirements.

entities.name: Bit-field layout
entities.description: Implementation- and ABI-defined packing and allocation of language bit-fields.

entities.name: Enum representation
entities.description: Rules determining an enumeration's storage size and value representation.

entities.name: Boolean representation
entities.description: Representation and size of boolean-like values across language/platform boundaries.

entities.name: Pointer representation
entities.description: Size, representation, and interpretation of pointers under a platform ABI.

entities.name: Pointer width
entities.description: Number of bits in a pointer representation, not necessarily identical to all address widths.

entities.name: Endianness
entities.description: Byte order used to represent multibyte scalar values in memory.

entities.name: Floating-point representation
entities.description: Representation and calling conventions for floating-point values.

entities.name: Vector type ABI
entities.description: Representation and argument/result handling for vector or SIMD types.

entities.name: Long double
entities.description: C floating type whose size, format, alignment, and passing convention vary among ABIs.

entities.name: wchar_t
entities.description: Wide-character type whose width and encoding conventions vary across platforms.

entities.name: size_t
entities.description: Unsigned type used for object sizes, with width tied to the target data model.

entities.name: time_t
entities.description: Time representation type whose width or signedness choices can affect compatibility.

entities.name: intmax_t
entities.description: Integer type capable of representing any supported signed integer type, with ABI-sensitive representation.

entities.name: C++ object layout
entities.description: Rules for class subobjects, base classes, fields, padding, and object representation.

entities.name: Virtual method table (vtable)
entities.description: Implementation structure supporting virtual dispatch under a C++ ABI.

entities.name: Virtual table pointer (vptr)
entities.description: Pointer stored or otherwise associated with an object to enable virtual dispatch.

entities.name: Multiple inheritance
entities.description: C++ object model feature affecting subobject layout, pointer adjustment, and dispatch.

entities.name: Run-time type information (RTTI)
entities.description: Metadata and runtime mechanisms supporting dynamic type identification and casts.

entities.name: Template instantiation
entities.description: Compiler-generated specialization whose symbol naming and emitted representation affect linkage.

entities.name: Inline function
entities.description: Function that may be emitted in multiple translation units, with ODR and linkage constraints.

entities.name: One Definition Rule (ODR)
entities.description: C++ rule governing definitions across translation units; violations can cause undefined behavior or ABI trouble.

entities.name: Standard library ABI
entities.description: Binary interface of library types, symbols, layouts, and runtime behavior.

entities.name: libstdc++ dual ABI
entities.description: GCC C++ standard-library transition supporting old and new ABI variants for selected types.

entities.name: Microsoft Visual C++ ABI
entities.description: Microsoft C++ binary conventions used by MSVC toolchains, subject to toolchain/runtime compatibility.

entities.name: Itanium C++ ABI
entities.description: Widely used C++ ABI specification adopted by GCC and Clang on many non-Windows targets.

entities.name: System V ABI
entities.description: Family of platform binary conventions for Unix-like systems and multiple ISAs.

entities.name: AMD64 System V ABI
entities.description: System V AMD64 ABI covering calling convention, data model, stack, object and runtime conventions.

entities.name: Microsoft x64 ABI
entities.description: Windows x64 calling convention and related binary conventions.

entities.name: Windows ABI
entities.description: Windows platform binary contracts including calling conventions, system interfaces, object format, and runtime constraints.

entities.name: Linux ABI
entities.description: Linux userspace/kernel and library binary contracts for a specific architecture and environment.

entities.name: Linux system-call ABI
entities.description: Architecture-specific interface for entering the Linux kernel, including syscall numbers and argument conventions.

entities.name: System call
entities.description: Controlled transition from user code to kernel services using a platform-defined convention.

entities.name: System-call number
entities.description: Number identifying a kernel service in an architecture-specific system-call ABI.

entities.name: System-call wrapper
entities.description: Library or assembly stub exposing system calls through a callable interface.

entities.name: Kernel ABI
entities.description: Binary interface exposed by a kernel, including any supported stability commitments.

entities.name: Kernel-to-userspace ABI
entities.description: Boundary conventions for user processes interacting with the kernel.

entities.name: Userspace ABI
entities.description: Binary conventions governing application and library execution in user mode.

entities.name: Linux Standard Base (LSB)
entities.description: Specification set historically defining parts of Linux application binary and library interfaces.

entities.name: Intel Binary Compatibility Standard (iBCS)
entities.description: Historical binary compatibility specification for Unix-like x86 environments.

entities.name: Embedded ABI (EABI)
entities.description: ABI profile for embedded systems specifying data, calls, object files, and register/stack conventions.

entities.name: ARM EABI
entities.description: Embedded ABI family for Arm targets, with variants and floating-point conventions.

entities.name: ARM OABI
entities.description: Older Arm Linux ABI conventions, distinct from the newer EABI usage.

entities.name: PowerPC EABI
entities.description: Embedded ABI conventions for PowerPC targets.

entities.name: MIPS EABI
entities.description: Embedded ABI conventions for MIPS targets.

entities.name: Hard-float ABI
entities.description: ABI variant passing eligible floating-point arguments/results in hardware floating-point registers.

entities.name: Soft-float ABI
entities.description: ABI variant using integer registers or memory conventions rather than hardware FP argument registers.

entities.name: Softfp ABI
entities.description: Convention that may use software-compatible calling conventions while allowing hardware floating-point instructions.

entities.name: Target triple
entities.description: Toolchain identifier typically encoding architecture, vendor, operating system, and environment/ABI details.

entities.name: Compiler flags
entities.description: Options that can change code generation, data layout, calling convention, or ABI-relevant features.

entities.name: CPU feature flags
entities.description: Options enabling instruction extensions; some may alter vector types or call boundaries.

entities.name: Preprocessor definitions
entities.description: Compile-time definitions that can change declarations or data layout across translation units.

entities.name: Header file
entities.description: Declarations and type definitions used to compile clients against an API.

entities.name: Library version
entities.description: Release identifier for a library; compatibility depends on preserved binary-visible behavior.

entities.name: Semantic versioning
entities.description: Version-labeling convention often used to communicate intended compatibility changes, but not a guarantee by itself.

entities.name: SONAME
entities.description: ELF shared-library identity used by dynamic linkers to select compatible library names.

entities.name: DLL
entities.description: Dynamically linked library format/concept in Windows environments.

entities.name: Import library
entities.description: Link-time artifact describing or forwarding imports from a DLL.

entities.name: Application manifest
entities.description: Metadata that can influence Windows runtime activation or dependency behavior.

entities.name: Dynamic symbol
entities.description: Symbol exported or looked up across dynamically linked components.

entities.name: Weak symbol
entities.description: Symbol definition or reference with weaker resolution precedence under toolchain rules.

entities.name: Exported symbol set
entities.description: Set of externally visible symbols forming part of a library's binary surface.

entities.name: Opaque pointer
entities.description: Pointer to an implementation-hidden object, reducing client dependence on private layout.

entities.name: PImpl idiom
entities.description: C++ technique hiding implementation layout behind a pointer to reduce ABI exposure.

entities.name: Stable C wrapper
entities.description: C-compatible façade around a library implementation to constrain cross-language ABI surface.

entities.name: Versioned API
entities.description: Source interface evolution strategy; API versioning alone does not ensure ABI compatibility.

entities.name: ABI versioning
entities.description: Explicit identification or coexistence of binary interface revisions.

entities.name: Backward compatibility
entities.description: Newer provider remains usable by older consumers under specified conditions.

entities.name: Forward compatibility
entities.description: Older provider can support newer consumers only when the contract explicitly allows it.

entities.name: Cross-compilation
entities.description: Building binaries on one host for a different target platform.

entities.name: Cross-language linking
entities.description: Linking components produced from different programming languages through compatible conventions.

entities.name: Mixed-compiler linking
entities.description: Linking object code generated by different compiler implementations or versions.

entities.name: Undefined behavior
entities.description: Program behavior for which the language contract imposes no requirements; ABI mismatch can expose such failures.

entities.name: Marshalling
entities.description: Converting values and data structures to a representation suitable for a foreign runtime or call boundary.

entities.name: Foreign data layout
entities.description: Representation requirements for values crossing a language or process boundary.

entities.name: Callback
entities.description: Call from a foreign library/runtime back into a client-provided function.

entities.name: Thread-local storage (TLS)
entities.description: ABI mechanisms for per-thread variables and their access models.

entities.name: Thread-local variable model
entities.description: Compiler/linker/runtime strategy for locating thread-local data.

entities.name: Process startup
entities.description: Entry-point and initialization conventions before application-level main or equivalent.

entities.name: Entry point
entities.description: Address or symbol where a loader or runtime begins program execution.

entities.name: Initialization and finalization
entities.description: Conventions for constructors, destructors, and runtime startup/teardown.

entities.name: Constructor array
entities.description: ELF metadata mechanism used to run initialization functions.

entities.name: Termination handler
entities.description: Mechanism for cleanup and finalization during process termination.

entities.name: TLS destructor
entities.description: Cleanup mechanism for thread-local objects where supported.

entities.name: Signal frame
entities.description: OS-defined saved execution context used when delivering signals or analogous asynchronous events.

entities.name: Signal handler ABI
entities.description: Rules for entering and returning from signal handlers and accessing saved context.

entities.name: System register usage
entities.description: Rules governing special architectural registers or processor state at binary interfaces.

entities.name: Floating-point control state
entities.description: Rounding, exception, and vector state that may have preservation or call-boundary rules.

entities.name: Vector register preservation
entities.description: Rules governing which SIMD/vector registers must survive function calls.

entities.name: Redirection thunk
entities.description: Small adapter that translates between calling conventions, symbol forms, or instruction modes.

entities.name: Calling-convention adapter
entities.description: Generated or handwritten shim translating between ABI conventions.

entities.name: ABI conformance test
entities.description: Test suite checking calling, layout, symbol, unwind, or system-interface rules.

entities.name: ABI diff tool
entities.description: Tool comparing exported symbols, type layouts, or other binary interface details across versions.

entities.name: Symbol inspection tool
entities.description: Tool that lists or demangles symbols in object files and libraries.

entities.name: Disassembler
entities.description: Tool decoding machine code into instruction representations for inspection.

entities.name: libabigail
entities.description: Tooling ecosystem for comparing ABI changes in ELF binaries and libraries.

entities.name: abi-compliance-checker
entities.description: Tool for checking library ABI compatibility using binary and debug information.

entities.name: Application software vendor (ISV)
entities.description: Software provider that depends on platform ABI stability to distribute binaries.

entities.name: Operating-system vendor
entities.description: Provider responsible for platform and kernel/library binary interfaces.

entities.name: Library maintainer
entities.description: Maintains library binary surfaces and compatibility policy.

entities.name: Compiler vendor
entities.description: Maintains code generation and ABI behavior across compiler versions.

entities.name: Endianness conversion
entities.description: Explicit conversion when binary data crosses environments with different byte-order expectations.

entities.name: Serialization format
entities.description: Explicit representation for data exchange that is independent of in-process ABI layout.

entities.name: Network protocol
entities.description: Specified wire-level communication contract, distinct from an in-process ABI.

entities.name: IPC
entities.description: Inter-process communication interface, usually distinct from an in-process ABI.

entities.name: Shared-memory interface
entities.description: Cross-component data exchange through shared memory whose layout, synchronization, and ownership rules must be specified.

entities.name: ABI surface
entities.description: All binary-visible symbols, layouts, calling rules, metadata, and runtime behavior exposed to consumers.

entities.name: ABI risk assessment
entities.description: Evaluation of proposed changes for binary compatibility impact.

entities.name: ABI policy
entities.description: Project rules defining supported compatibility scope, versioning, and deprecation.

entities.name: Rebuild requirement
entities.description: Need to recompile dependent consumers after an incompatible interface change.

entities.name: Runtime crash
entities.description: Failure symptom that can result from mismatched calling conventions or data layouts.

entities.name: Silent data corruption
entities.description: Incorrect behavior caused by mismatched structure layout, parameter classification, or type representation.

entities.name: Link-time failure
entities.description: Unresolved symbols or incompatible object metadata prevent successful linking.

entities.name: Load-time failure
entities.description: Dynamic loader cannot locate or resolve required libraries, symbols, or versions.

entities.name: Cross-platform portability
entities.description: Ability to move source or binaries between platforms; ABI portability is narrower and more constrained than source portability.

entities.name: Reproducible build
entities.description: Build process yielding equivalent artifacts from controlled inputs; relevant to validating ABI changes.

entities.name: ABI documentation
entities.description: Human-readable contract for supported data layouts, calling conventions, symbols, and platform boundaries.

relationships.description: API is source-level; ABI governs compiled-code interaction.
ABI compatibility depends on target hardware, operating system, and toolchain.
ABI is associated with a target ISA and its architectural conventions.
Calling conventions are a central ABI component.
ABI specifies type size, alignment, and aggregate layout.
A complete platform ABI commonly defines or relies on object formats.
OS ABI defines how applications invoke kernel services.
Language ABIs may define symbol naming.
Some language ABIs define exception propagation and unwinding.
Libraries expose binary interfaces as part of the platform's usable ABI surface.
Long-lived binary distribution depends on preserving stable contracts.
Compatible binary interfaces allow precompiled components to interoperate.
Source-compatible changes help consumers rebuild, but do not guarantee binary compatibility.
An incompatible binary-visible change breaks prior assumptions.
Consumers may need recompilation or coordinated upgrades.
Symbol or metadata mismatches can prevent linking.
Call or layout mismatches can fail at runtime.
Mismatched layouts may silently misinterpret values.
Specification records ABI rules.
Compiler, runtime, OS, and libraries implement the contract.
Toolchain target configuration must match the intended platform.
Compiler-generated calls and function prologues follow calling conventions.
Assembler emits object code and metadata.
Linker combines object files.
Linker matches symbol references to definitions.
Linker applies relocations when producing output.
Loader maps and prepares executable artifacts.
Dynamic linker resolves shared-library dependencies.
Static linking incorporates selected object code from archives.
Dynamic linking resolves code in shared objects or DLLs.
Object files follow a format specification.
ELF is an object/executable file format.
PE/COFF describes object and executable formats used in Windows ecosystems.
Mach-O is an object and executable format.
Wasm modules are binary artifacts but target a virtual execution environment.
Object files contain symbol tables or related symbol metadata.
Symbols are recorded in symbol tables.
Resolution binds references to definitions.
Visibility rules help determine the externally visible interface.
Dynamic symbols can be associated with version identifiers.
Mangling maps language-level names/signatures to linker-visible names.
Demanglers render mangled symbols in readable form.
A relocation entry encodes a relocation operation.
PIC facilitates loading code at different addresses.
PLT stubs can participate in lazy or dynamic symbol resolution.
GOT entries may be initialized or updated for dynamic addresses.
Convention determines argument locations and classification.
Convention determines result locations.
Call boundary specifies which register values caller must protect.
Callee preserves required nonvolatile registers.
Call convention governs stack-frame organization.
Stack alignment requirements are ABI-defined.
Variadic calls need defined argument classification and metadata rules.
ABI rules determine direct versus indirect aggregate return.
Some conventions specify preservation of vector state.
Calls must use matching conventions at the binary boundary.
Returns follow the agreed result and saved-state rules.
Nested calls commonly create frames on the call stack.
Stack pointer identifies current stack position.
Frame pointer may provide stable frame-relative addressing.
Some ABIs reserve a stack region for leaf-function use.
Some conventions require caller-reserved home space.
Type classes determine register or memory locations.
Classification algorithms assign values to eligible register classes.
Indirect aggregate returns may use a hidden result pointer.
Tail calls require compatible argument, stack, and return conventions.
Unwind metadata enables restoration of caller state.
Nonlocal jumps restore a saved execution context but are not ordinary exception unwinding.
Exception propagation relies on language/runtime-specific binary rules.
Unwinders may consult language-specific personality routines.
Unwind tables store frame-recovery information.
Debug metadata may be embedded or associated with object artifacts.
Foreign calls require compatible calling conventions.
Cross-language values must have compatible layouts or be marshalled.
Bindings make foreign functions accessible to a language.
Many language FFIs use C-compatible functions as an interoperability baseline.
The declaration requests C-linkage conventions where supported.
C++ ABI specifies names for overloaded and otherwise distinct entities.
